summary: One required finding: the required closure-only command tree must be explicitly distinguished from the root-command claim that D4/EE-5a refuses. The role table, schema copy and structural binding otherwise check out.

requiredFindings.problem: The closure-only commands rule removes mounting and dispatch but leaves the retained DR-103 meaning of the required command tree as a request to mount a root command. D4/EE-5a refuses the claim at admission, before a mount can occur. Thus a first-party grammar manifest with the mandatory parentless command can still be classified as an excluded root-command claim. The README answers whether it will be mounted, which does not decide whether it claims a root command. The contract needs an explicit role-scoped interpretation of the required tree and its D4 join.

evidence.text: The declarative command grammar this component asks the host to mount. The ROOT namespace is host-owned and flat: exactly one entry may omit 'parent' and that entry is the component's mounted root command; every other entry must name a parent within this manifest. The component declares; the host owns all parsing and dispatch; discovery never hands a component raw root parser authority. Help/completion/inventory are served from this declaration without executing component code.
EE-5a: a manifest claiming a project hook, root command or contribution-granted probe is refused at R10a.
The excluded input is a component manifest claiming a project hook, root command, or contribution-granted probe; refusal is at admission.
The successor preserves all other DR-103 rules. The grammar example retains its required root command; the D4 explanation relies solely on the command never being mounted.

nonBlockingObservations.problem: CR-T4 proposes refusing symlink entrypoints for every role. The existing analyzer owner resolves an entrypoint through in-tree symlinks and then checks the resolved file and executable bits; CMC:125 also says entrypoints resolve to executable files. The new regular-file naming rule is stated for closure-only roles. This control therefore proposes an additional analyzer restriction beyond the role-scoped change and the stated preservation of existing rules.

The no-component-launch rule, empty capabilities/permissions and non-executable regular-file entrypoint are appropriate for the four retained-byte roles; tools within a tree still require their own D launch law. Those words do not require a closure-only role to open a provider session.
